chapter: Postwar years, accident and lean times
title: The old style still struggles; family reunion in Hamburg
summary: The bebop shift still affects his work, though audiences in Hamburg suggest a revival; he met his daughter, her husband the colonel and their children there.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: But in any event, so after -- after you came back to New York from Philadelphia you were faced with this prospect that there was another kind of jazz that was getting a lot more attention than what you had been play-
ing, and was -- Yeah, yeah.
How long did -- how long did that go on affecting you, and affecting --
Affecting me?
Yeah.
Well, oh --
As far as jobs were concerned, and where you -- how much you could work?
Well up until now it still does.
It still does.
But a lot of the people have been able to shake it.
Yeah. Because I think, as you are talking about these kids over in Germany that the attitudes are changing, they're rediscovering the kind of thing that you've been doing all you-life.
Yes. Yeah, yeah. I've got it there, why can't I think what it is? So and so ham --
Hamburg?
Hamburg, Germany.
Hamburg, Germany. That was the town?
That's just where it was, because I brought -- I've got a good friend of mine, I brought him some cigars to his home. I brought him cigars, some cigars back,

you know, from Hamburg. And that's a big place, and man, it was jumping, oh! It was jumping. It was terrific. And the meantime, my daughters -- my daughter was there with her husband, who's general -- not general, uh, uh, he was a major, and then what's the next after major? Colonel.
Colonel. Right.
He's a colonel now. He's over in the -- where all that mess is going on now, got -- God I hope he gets back safely.
Vietnam. That's theoretically over now. Is that what you mean?
Yeah, but I hope he gets back here.
Well, they're supposed to be all out by now.

Yeah, well I hope so. And he was there, in Hamburg, with my daughter, and two children. And we had a ball. We met, I was doing (unintelligible) a concert over there, and they came over, and we got together, saw each other, and whatnot.
But as I was telling you, that too is -- well it wasn't -- it was a little on the -- between, you know, on both sides. The guys with all that hair and stuff on their face, and they were playing --
It's a whole new world.
Yeah, you know.
